title: Kansas City Chiefs Unveil $3 Billion Domed Stadium Set to Open in Kansas by 2031
excerpt: The franchise released first renderings of a 70,000-seat enclosed venue in Wyandotte County, designed to preserve Arrowhead's legacy while bidding for Super Bowls and other major events.
body:
• The Chiefs revealed renderings of a $3 billion fully enclosed domed stadium in Kansas, designed by Kansas City-based firms MANICA and HNTB, with a planned opening for the 2031 NFL season.
  • The 70,000-seat venue will feature a translucent ETFE polymer roof and a seating bowl modeled after the iconic Arrowhead Stadium, which the Chiefs have called home since 1972.
  • Kansas lawmakers voted unanimously to allow up to $1.8 billion in STAR bonds for the project, with the Hunt family committing $1 billion in additional development.
  • The franchise plans to bid on hosting a Super Bowl, Final Four, College Football Playoff games, and future FIFA World Cup matches once the new stadium opens.

The Kansas City Chiefs on Wednesday released the first renderings of their new stadium, a $3 billion domed venue in Wyandotte County, Kansas, that will replace the storied Arrowhead Stadium when it opens for the 2031 NFL season.

The design, led by Kansas City-based architecture firm MANICA with HNTB serving as architect of record, features a fully enclosed structure with a ceiling made of translucent ethylene tetrafluoroethylene (ETFE) panels. The transparent roof will shield fans from Kansas City's brutal winter weather while preserving natural light and, as the team emphasized, "maximizing visibility for military flyovers."

"From the beginning, our goal has been to build something that improved the gameday experience for every single fan. This new stadium will do just that. It's spectacular."

— Clark Hunt, Chiefs Chairman and CEO

Arrowhead's Legacy, Reimagined

The renderings show a structure that deliberately echoes Arrowhead's distinctive profile. The dome will feature a symmetrical, curved exterior with scalloped upper decks in each end zone, a signature architectural element of the 1972-built stadium that has defined the franchise's visual identity for over five decades.

Inside, the seating bowl mirrors Arrowhead's configuration. The Chiefs' Ring of Honor will be prominently placed above the bowl, and the Hall of Honor will be twice the size of the current one. The team store is expected to be four times larger. A "Drum Deck" for pregame and in-game ceremonies has also been incorporated into the design.

Hunt said the stadium will seat 70,000 fans and was designed with one clear priority from season-ticket holders: noise. In 2014, Arrowhead regained the Guinness World Record for loudest stadium when fans generated 142.2 decibels during a game against the New England Patriots.

"While we're still finalizing many of the details, there are a few things we know for sure: it will hold 70,000 fans, it will still be the best place in the world to tailgate, and the whole building will be built for noise."

— Clark Hunt, Chiefs Chairman and CEO

The Money Behind the Move

The stadium's financing took shape in late December when Kansas lawmakers voted unanimously to allow sales tax and revenue (STAR) bonds covering up to 70 percent of the project's cost. That amounts to approximately $1.8 billion in taxpayer-backed funding, according to NBC Sports, covering the stadium and an accompanying mixed-use district that includes a new training facility.

Hunt and his family have committed $1 billion in additional development, a portion of which will be incentivized through the STAR bonds program. The project will also include more than 20,000 parking spots surrounding the venue, preserving the tailgating culture that has been central to the Chiefs' game-day identity.

The projected location sits near the Kansas Speedway and The Legends entertainment district in Wyandotte County, roughly 25 miles west of Arrowhead. The area already hosts Children's Mercy Park, home of MLS club Sporting Kansas City.

Super Bowl Ambitions

Beyond NFL Sundays, the enclosed venue opens the door to hosting events that Kansas City has never been able to bid on. Hunt said the franchise plans to pursue a Super Bowl, NCAA Final Fours, College Football Playoff games, and bowl games starting in 2032.

The stadium's playing surface is also being designed to accommodate a FIFA-regulation pitch without the costly modifications Arrowhead required to host 2026 World Cup matches. "When the World Cup comes back in 25 or 30 years, the field will be designed so that we don't have to do the work that we had to do to expand the field's width on Arrowhead," Hunt said during the NFL Draft earlier this year.

What's Next

The Chiefs' lease at Arrowhead with Jackson County, Missouri, runs through the end of the 2031 season. The design competition between MANICA and Populous concluded with Wednesday's announcement, with MANICA winning the lead design role. CAA ICON is serving as the owner's representative on the project.

Chiefs President Mark Donovan called it a "transformational stadium undertaking" that would unfold over the next five years. Construction timelines and a final site selection within Wyandotte County have not been publicly confirmed, though the franchise has consistently pointed to the Kansas Speedway area as the preferred location.

Not all fans are sold. Reaction on social media ranged from excitement to criticism that the new venue resembles other recently built NFL stadiums, particularly the Las Vegas Raiders' Allegiant Stadium, which MANICA also designed. "Is it just me or are all these NFL stadiums looking identical?" one fan wrote on X.

The Chiefs, four-time Super Bowl champions, are betting $3 billion that their version will stand apart.
